text: This guide explains how taxes work in Germany, and how to pay less taxes.

section: The taxes you pay in Germany
text: All German residents must pay taxes. These are the taxes to pay: Income and wage tax ( Einkommensteuer, Lohnsteuer) Health insurance ( Krankenversicherung) Long-term care insurance ( Pflegeversicherung) Public pension insurance ( gesetzliche Rentenversicherung) Unemployment insurance ( Arbeitslosenversicherung) Church tax ( Kirchensteuer) Solidarity surcharge ( Solidaritätszuschlag) If you are an employee, your employer collects taxes directly from your paycheck. If you are self-employed, you pay taxes by bank transfer or direct debit. Income from investments is taxed differently. [§ 32d EStG] You pay: Capital gains tax ( Kapitalertragsteuer) Church tax ( Kirchensteuer) Solidarity surcharge ( Solidaritätszuschlag)

section: The taxes you pay in Germany
title: Income and wage tax
text: All German residents pay income tax ( Einkommensteuer). This tax is a percentage of your income. It’s a progressive tax, so if you earn more, you pay a bigger percentage of your income. [§ 32a EStG] If you earn less than € 12,348 per year, you pay no income tax. If you earn the median income, your income tax is around 18% of your income. The maximum income tax is 45% of your income. [§ 32a EStG] If you are an employee, you pay a wage tax ( Lohnsteuer) on every paycheck. This is a prepayment of your estimated income tax. If you pay too much wage tax, you can make a tax declaration and get money back. Usually, tips are not taxed.

section: The taxes you pay in Germany
title: Health insurance
text: All German residents must have health insurance ( Krankenversicherung). Health insurance pays for your healthcare when you are sick. There are three types of health insurance: Public health insurance. It costs a percentage of your income. Private health insurance. The cost is set by the health insurer. Expat health insurance. The cost is set by the health insurer. If you are an employee, your employer pays half of it. If you earn less than € 565 per month, you can use your parents’ or spouse’s health insurance for free. Students get a cheaper tariff. Calculate the cost of German health insurance and see health insurance options for employees, students and freelancers. This tool requires JavaScript to work. section: The taxes you pay in Germany
title: Long-term care insurance
text: Long-term care insurance ( Pflegeversicherung) pays for your healthcare when you are old. It costs 2.6% to 4.2% of your income. If you have a job, your employer pays 1.8% and you pay the rest. Use my health insurance calculator to calculate your Pflegeversicherung.

section: The taxes you pay in Germany
title: Public pension insurance
text: All employees must pay into the public pension system. It costs 18.6% of your income. If you are an employee, your employer pays half of it, so you pay 9.3%. If you are self-employed, public pension insurance is usually optional. If you don’t pay public pension insurance, you must make your own retirement plans.

section: The taxes you pay in Germany
title: Unemployment insurance
text: Unemployment insurance ( Arbeitslosenversicherung) pays a percentage of your salary if you lose your job. It costs 1.3% of your income. The maximum cost is € 109.85 per month.

section: The taxes you pay in Germany
title: Church tax
text: If you are a member of certain churches, you pay a church tax. It’s a percentage of your income tax. You also pay church tax on investment income. If you live in Baden-Württemberg or Bavaria, it’s 8% of your income tax. In other states it’s 9% of your income tax. You stop paying church tax by leaving the church.

section: The taxes you pay in Germany
title: Solidarity surcharge
text: If you pay more than € 20,350 per year in income tax, you must pay a solidarity surcharge ( Solidaritätszuschlag). It’s a percentage of your income tax. You also pay a solidarity surcharge on investment income. German tax calculator

section: The taxes you pay in Germany
title: Capital gains tax
text: The capital gains tax ( Kapitalertragsteuer) is a 25% tax on profits from investments. It applies to profit, interests and dividends from stocks, ETFs and other investments. It does not apply to cryptocurrencies. The first € 1,000 per year are tax-free. Most German brokers deduct this tax automatically when you sell stocks or receive dividends. You must also pay church tax and a solidarity surcharge on investments.

All German households must pay the TV tax. If you run a business, you might need to pay the trade tax. Most things you buy have the value added tax included in the price. There is also the vehicle tax, the dog tax, property tax and a few others.

If you are self-employed, you must pay… Income tax Health insurance Long-term care insurance Church tax Solidarity surcharge You can choose to pay… Unemployment insurance. If you don’t pay for it, and you don’t get unemployment benefits. Public pension insurance. If you don’t pay for it, and you don’t get a public pension. You must make your own retirement plans. Your business must also pay… Trade tax – More information Value Added Tax (VAT) – More information IHK membership fee (if you have a Gewerbe) – Fee calculator Cost of running a business Since you are self-employed, your employer does not pay half of your health insurance, pension insurance or unemployment insurance. This means that you pay twice as much for social contributions.

Your tax class affects how your wage tax is calculated. It does not affect how much income tax you pay. It only changes how much income tax you pay in advance, as wage tax. You can change your tax class online with ELSTER. If you are self-employed, you might not have a tax class, because you don’t need to calculate your wage tax. There are 6 tax classes: Tax class 1 If you are not married, and you are not in any other tax class. Tax class 2 If you are not married, and you raise children alone. You get more tax benefits. Tax class 3 If you are married, and you earn more than your spouse. If you are in tax class 3, your spouse is in tax class 5. Tax class 4 If you are married, and you and your spouse have similar incomes. If you are in tax class 4, your spouse is also in tax class 4. Tax class 5 If you are married, and you earn less than your spouse. If you are in tax class 5, your spouse is in tax class 3. Tax class 6 This is the tax class for a second job. If you don’t have a tax ID, your employer might put you in tax class 6. You have no tax benefits, and you pay more wage tax.
